svg.title: Abstract Factory
svg.desc: Abstract Factory. Create families of related objects through one interface, so swapping the whole family never touches client code. Step 1, Hard-coded and mixable: ReceiptService calls new on S3 and SQS itself; a half-done Azure move pairs S3 with Service Bus. Step 2, One factory per family: ReceiptService gets an InfraFactory at startup and asks it for both products, so they always match. Step 3, Swap the whole family: issue(1001) runs on AWS, then Azure, then in memory for a test: only INFRA at startup changes. Step 4, Add families, not products: GcpFactory adds a family with no edits; createCache() would change InfraFactory and every factory.

g.text: ReceiptService calls new on S3 and SQS itself; a half-done Azure move pairs S3 with Service Bus.
ReceiptService gets an InfraFactory at startup and asks it for both products, so they always match.
issue(1001) runs on AWS, then Azure, then in memory for a test: only INFRA at startup changes.
GcpFactory adds a family with no edits; createCache() would change InfraFactory and every factory.
moving to Azure: 1 of 4 new calls edited
issue() now stores in S3 but sends to Service Bus:
a mixed family that nothing in the code prevents
and gets both products from one
a new family: three classes, no edits
a new product edits the interface
and all four factories, and every
family needs its own Cache class
Every new is another edit, and nothing stops a half-done move from mixing clouds
but a cloud-neutral port drifts toward the lowest common denominator
